messages:
eva: Heads-up: customer asked for HSM certification evidence and a short checklist we can hand them for BYOK onboarding. Can someone pull together what we can share without exposing ops detail?
jonah: I can draft the ops checklist. Quick Q: do they want FIPS validation docs or just SOC2/HSM provider attestation?
eva: They specified FIPS 140-2/3 level and HSM vendor attestation. Also asked about our RBAC model for key access and audit logs retention.
priya: For HSM specifics we can share vendor FIPS cert, manufacturing attestation, and PKCS#11/CryptoAPI compatibility statement. Don't include our internal module configs.
luis: Legal prefers a redacted export: vendor cert + statement of custody boundaries, plus statement that customer keys are not exported from their keystore. Avoid any playbooks or service account names.
kim: On RBAC: we should provide a high-level diagram and list of roles that can request key operations (create/import/rotate/backup/restore). Example roles: CustomerAdmin (owns key), HSMAdmin (operational, no key material access), Auditor (readonly).
jonah: To be concrete, I'll add the allowed ops matrix (who can call Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign/Export). We should also note multi-person approval for key export if it's ever allowed.
priya: Note: we do envelope encryption in the platform. Root CMKs live in customer HSM (BYOK) or our managed KMS when customer opts in. Application-level data keys are ephemeral and kept in RAM only.
priya: Small snippet we can include for technical teams:
```
# sample pkcs11 check (do not run against prod HSM)
pkcs11-tool --module /usr/local/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so --list-objects
```
jonah: Audit logging: customers asked about retention. We currently retain HSM audit trail events 1 year by default for Dedicated, 90 days for Hosted (can extend). Need to note that logs are WORM and hashed for tamper-evidence.
kim: We should include how logs surface in Console (per-key audit view + raw export). Also include the alerting SLA for suspicious key usage: pager within 15m for high-severity anomalies.
eva: Vulnerability triage notes: if CVE affects HSM firmware we do: 1) validate vendor advisory, 2) escalate to infra oncall, 3) schedule patch window on Dedicated/non-customer-isolated pools, 4) notify impacted customers and provide mitigation. Add sample incident timeline.
luis: For compliance, include statement about evidence we can provide for auditors: vendor certs, attestation letters, key custody diagram, RBAC matrix, and anonymized audit sample events. We cannot provide raw key material.
priya: Integration notes for KMS: describe the envelope flow, HKDF derivation, and how we do key wrapping. Mention supported algorithms (RSA-OAEP-256, AES-GCM wrap) and fallback to software-wrapping if HSM not available.
jonah: Does anyone have a short blurb about key ceremony/escrow? Customer asked about who holds escrow.
priya: We recommend split-escrow only if required. If escrowed, we use 3-of-5 quorum and HSM-backed key shares; ceremony is recorded and attested by a third party. Keep description non-sensitive.
kim: I'll assemble a one‑page "what we share" and a separate ops-facing checklist for internal use. @luis can you confirm legal wording?
luis: Will review. Also suggest adding a revocation/rotation FAQ for auditors (timing, rotation proof, rewrap steps).
deploy-bot: [deploy] created doc draft: /internal/sec/hsm_byo_playback_v1 (restricted).
eva: Great — let's aim to have the customer-facing packet ready by EOD PST. If anyone has red-flag phrases we should avoid, post them here.
jonah: Avoid operational usernames, internal ticket numbers, and playbook runbooks.
priya: Also avoid screenshots of HSM consoles.
kim: I'll ping a draft in #eng-security-review when done :thumbsup:
luis: Thanks all.
